prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas with exactly two side-by-side cells, TOP then BOTTOM, for the same soot-stained brick open doorway shown in the attached reference sheet. The native source alone controls material and identity: reddish soot-stained brick piers, charcoal masonry, pale tan stone arch/lintel, central open black passage. The current source-plus-six sheet supplies the accepted FRONT, RIGHT, LEFT and REAR. The Iron Tracks open doorway plan images are geometry-only examples for shallow doorway footprints; do not copy their materials.

The physical doorway is an upright open arch with shallow wall thickness, broad X width and narrow Y depth. TOP is viewed straight down (+Z); BOTTOM straight up from below (-Z). Both views must be true shallow plan/end-surface projections: broad width across the arch, small depth matching the accepted side elevations. Keep the central passage open as a dark elongated gap; show two side piers at the correct ends and the pale stone lintel/arch cap spanning the opening. Do not draw the full front-facing arch, stacked red brick courses, tall pillars, or a four-corner display panel. No upright door face or bricks visible as vertical front panels.

TOP: pale tan/gray stone upper lintel/crown cap across the doorway, flat brick pier tops at both sides, dark open passage footprint, and subtle charcoal interior rim. BOTTOM: opaque shallow underside of the pale stone lintel and matching pier footing/base cross-sections, with the same dark open passage gap; no top-facing arch face or stacked brick shafts. Preserve the same orientation and footprint in both cells. Center each isolated view, generous transparent margins, no labels or shadows, no cell bleed; crisp Pocket Dungeon pixel-art clusters.
